messages:
morgan: FYI rolling kernel upgrade (6.2.14) started in us-west on the A100 pool, seeing unexpected NVLink topology changes and degraded inter-GPU perf on ~18 nodes.
cheng: Which nodes? any pattern by chassis or rack?
ops-bot: deploy-bot: started upgrade job upgrade-kernel-usw-a100-2026-03-27 on 24 nodes - batch 1 of 4.
noah: hitting NCCL errors in internal stress tests on two nodes, sample error: "NCCL WARN Network : AllGather failed, unhandled system error". perf for allreduce down ~6-8x.
tara: quick check: nvidia-smi topo -m shows NVLink links marked as X (not NVLink) on affected hosts, looks like fallback to PCIe.
morgan: paste of a quick snip from one affected host:
```
# lspci | grep -i nvidia
0000:af:00.0 VGA compatible controller: NVIDIA Corporation A100-SXM4-40GB

# nvidia-smi topo -m
        GPU0    GPU1    CPU Affinity
GPU0     X      PCIe    0-39
GPU1    PCIe     X      0-39
```
cheng: dmesg shows NVLink link down msgs around kernel init: "nvlink: peer link training failed, disabling NVLink on GPU1". also saw ACS/PCIe error frames.
noah: this smells like a kernel driver handshake change breaking the NVLink firmware path when combined with driver 535.45. Make/verify: cuda 12.1 + driver 535 variants reported OK elsewhere but maybe kernel bits removed a compat shim.
tara: impact: jobs on these nodes drop throughput, queued inference latency spikes in us-west by ~30% for large context batch workloads; might exhaust our capacity headroom.
morgan: immediate mitigation: cordon affected nodes, migrate live inference shards to adjacent racks (we have 10 spare nodes in region), pause next upgrade batch. ops-bot, can you pause batch 2?
ops-bot: deploy-bot: paused upgrade job upgrade-kernel-usw-a100-2026-03-27, batch 2/4 held. Marking nodes with tag kernel-rollback-check.
cheng: need a repro matrix: kernel version, driver build, nvlink fw, and whether PCIe ACS was toggled by the hypervisor. who wants to run NVLink diagnostic across the pool?
noah: I'll run nccl-tests + nvlink-diagnostics on the affected 18 nodes (starting now). Will post logs to /infra/ops/nvlink-issues/1769504321.
tara: ops playbook suggestion: if NVLink can't be restored quickly, prefer rolling rollback to prior kernel (6.1.x) on affected batch and redeploy driver variant verified in staging. estimate 45-60m per batch.
morgan: agree. also opening an incident doc so support/pgs can triage customer-facing latency. tagging @oncall for rota.
noah: quick grep of NCCL log shows repeated "unreachable peer" + group reinit attempts, looks like peeraccess wasn't negotiated.
cheng: can someone check nvlink fw versions? I want to rule out firmware mismatch from prior driver auto-updates.
morgan: noted. I'll coordinate fw check and schedule rollback for tonight's maintenance window if diagnostics confirm.
tara: add cost note: if we keep degraded nodes for >3h we'll burn through extra burst capacity in other regions; ops finance flagged potential $8k/day spike.
morgan: good point — prioritize rollback to protect cost and latency. updates as we have them. :warning:
